page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v5 is an ARM64-based general-purpose server belonging to the DPDSv5 family. It is powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor with 48 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz, featuring a single-thread-per-core architecture. The server is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It includes 1843 GB of local SSD storage and is premium storage capable, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks show a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves a strong multi-core CPU performance rating in stress-ng (85110.68) and a strong score in software compilation with Clang (39488.0). However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by Geekbench single-core (1121.0) and bzip3 single-threaded decompression (8.9 GB/sec) results. Memory bandwidth remains average across both small cached blocks (3316.13 GB/sec) and large uncached blocks (175.53 GB/sec read, 76.31 GB/sec write).

The ARM64 architecture offers high resource density and power efficiency, translating to qualitative cost advantages for highly parallelized workloads. However, the lack of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX, AMX, and BMI2 represents a tradeoff for legacy applications or workloads relying on these vector extensions. The server is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference, but is less optimal for single-threaded or heavy vector-math applications.
